Class 3 · Chapter 1 of 10

Thousands and number names

Read and say four-digit numbers like 4265, compare them and round them.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

By the end I can…

  • I can build and name a four-digit number.
  • I can order and round numbers.
  • I can solve a number clue.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 5

Four digits, four places

4265 has four digits: 4 thousands, 2 hundreds, 6 tens and 5 ones.

The 4 is worth 4000. It is the biggest part of the number.

Screen 2 of 5

Say the number name

Say the thousands, then the hundreds, then the tens and ones.

4265 is "four thousand two hundred and sixty-five".

Screen 3 of 5

Order numbers

Compare the thousands first. Then hundreds, then tens, then ones.

4265 and 4256 match until the tens. 6 tens is more than 5 tens, so 4265 is bigger.

Screen 4 of 5

Round to the nearest ten

Look at the ones digit. 0 to 4 rounds down. 5 to 9 rounds up.

4263 has 3 ones, so it rounds down to 4260.

Screen 5 of 5

Solve a number clue

I have 4 thousands, 2 hundreds, 6 tens and 5 ones. What am I?

Put each digit in its place: 4265. A clue lock is solved one place at a time.

Words to know
thousand
Ten hundreds. 1000 is one thousand.
place value
The job a digit does: thousands, hundreds, tens or ones.
round
Change a number to the nearest ten, so it is easier to use.

For parents

What your child learns

A 3-digit number is greatest when its biggest digit is in the hundreds place. In 4-digit clues, digits and ranges shrink the choices. Use each clue to cross out numbers that cannot fit.

A common slip

Children often compare digits from the right or overlook a range. Compare the highest place first. Check each clue against the final answer.

5-minute home activity: Digit cards

  1. Write 4 digits on separate paper cards.
  2. Make the greatest and the smallest number.
  3. Write a clue about the digit sum and the ones digit.
  4. Ask someone to find your number.
